title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes 'figures', meaning closed parts of a stratified or tame space. The aim is a purely order-theoretic description of the lattice of figures in terms of its 'strates' or 'multistrates', in the spirit of the tame topology programme of the Esquisse d'un programme.

Setup from p.53. There is a poset (𝓕, ≤) satisfying C1:
- (a) 𝓕 is nonempty;
- (b) every family bounded above has a supremum.
Hence 𝓕 has a least element ∅ (the sup of the empty family), and every bounded family has a join.
An element F is irreducible if F = Sup_{i∈I} F_i implies F = F_i for some i. These are the completely join-irreducible elements, and ∅ is excluded because the empty family is allowed. The set of irreducibles is called M; these are the 'multistrates'.

This page.
1. Definition. The irreducible figures ≤ F are called the strates of F. Their set is written F̄ ⊂ M, which gives a map 𝓕 → 𝒫(M), F ↦ F̄.
2. Axiom C2. Every figure is the supremum of its strates: F = Sup_{X∈F̄} X.
3. Corollary 1. F ↦ F̄ is injective and is an order-isomorphism onto its image 𝓛 ⊂ 𝒫(M), ordered by inclusion. The page further claims that this isomorphism carries Sup_i to ⋃_i.
4. Corollary 2. The family 𝓛 of subsets of M satisfies:
   - (a) if A ∈ 𝓛 and A_i ∈ 𝓛 with A_i ⊂ A, then ⋃A_i ∈ 𝓛;
   - (b) every x ∈ M has a smallest A_x ∈ 𝓛 containing it (namely x̄), so 𝓛 covers M.

Next page. The converse: a family 𝓛 ⊂ 𝒫(M) satisfying (a), (b) and nonemptiness gives a poset satisfying C1 and C2. Its irreducibles are exactly the A_x, and A ∈ 𝓛 is recovered as {x : A_x ⊂ A}. M is then preordered by x ≤ y ⇔ A_x ⊂ A_y.

In modern terms this is a Birkhoff/Raney-type representation. A bounded-complete poset in which every element is a join of completely join-prime elements is isomorphic to a family of down-sets (an Alexandrov-type system) of the poset of those elements. Its purpose is to reduce the combinatorics of figures in a stratified space to the poset of (multi)strata ordered by closure/specialization, with figures corresponding to closed unions of strata.
errors: Corollaries 1 and 2 do not follow from C1+C2 with the stated definition of irreducible (complete join-irreducibility). What is needed is complete join-primeness (X ≤ Sup F_i ⇒ X ≤ F_i for some i), which amounts to an extra distributivity hypothesis.

Counterexample: the diamond lattice M3 = {0, a, b, c, 1}. It satisfies C1 and C2: the irreducibles are a, b, c, and 1 = a∨b∨c. Yet Sup(b, c) = 1 has strates {a, b, c} ≠ {b} ∪ {c}. The image 𝓛 = {∅, {a}, {b}, {c}, {a,b,c}} is not closed under bounded unions, so 'Sup ↦ ⋃' and Corollary 2(a) fail.
Injectivity and order-reflection in Corollary 1 are correct as stated.
The converse on p.55 is correct, because there the A_x are automatically join-prime for set-theoretic unions.

ideas.what: Axiomatization of the poset of 'figures': bounded joins exist, irreducible elements are called (multi)strates, and every figure is the join of its strates.
ideas.modern_name: Bounded-complete poset generated by completely join-irreducible elements; spatial/algebraic lattice representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Birkhoff (finite distributive lattices, 1937); G. Raney (completely distributive lattices, 1952–53)
ideas.where_published: Only the general tame topology programme appears, in Esquisse d'un programme §5; this axiomatization does not.

ideas.what: Representation of figures as a family of subsets of the set of strata, closed under bounded unions, with minimal members A_x (the closure of a stratum).
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov topology / down-set representation of a poset (stratification poset of a stratified space)
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Alexandrov (1937); Birkhoff duality; the face poset of stratifications is standard

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard order-theoretic representation (Birkhoff/Raney/Alexandrov), written as a first draft. It contains a small gap: join-irreducible is used where join-prime is needed. It is of historical interest only as part of the unpublished 1986 axiomatization of figures for tame topology.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the image reads 's'appellent les strates de F' (underlined 'strates'), not 'les atomes de F'. Similarly, line 3 should be 'L'ens. des strates de F sera noté F̄'.
Line 2 likely reads '(Donc, strates de F ⊂ ens. des multistrates)' rather than 'atomes de F = une multi-atome'.
In C2 'ses atomes' should be 'ses strates'.
'induit une iso de un ordonné de 𝓕 avec l'ens' is probably 'induit un iso d'ensembles ordonnés de 𝓕 avec l'ens. 𝓛 ⊂ 𝒫(M) formé des F̄'.
Corollary 2 reads 'L'ens 𝓛 des parties de M satisfait les conditions', with 'a) 𝓛 ≠ ∅' struck through.
There is a marginal annotation (illegible, possibly 'Ceci') at the left of Corollary 2.
